endorsements.quote: Participants were also strongly aligned on the need for future work to center affected users with lived experience in designing the solutions, for example, at-risk adolescents.

unlisted_practices: Develop cross-industry benchmarks for evaluating AI chatbot responses to suicide and self-harm rather than relying on labs measuring their own systems against their own rubrics.
Develop a collective set of best practices for what chatbots should do before, during, and after users are in crisis, including risk assessment and support.
Establish neutral third-party infrastructure that can hold sensitive interaction data and make it available to researchers without it residing inside any one lab.
Develop shared standards for warm handoffs that connect AI users in crisis to human support.
Establish a standing AI and mental health advisory group of labs, clinicians, evaluators, and people with lived experience.

Do not terminate crisis conversations with a bare hotline referral; have AI chatbots respond to suicide and self-harm disclosures with empathy, risk acknowledgment, and continued engagement consistent with clinical practice.
Evaluate chatbot safety in multi-turn conversations rather than only single-turn prompts, since guardrails degrade over long interactions.

screen.reason: This is a primer and framework document developed from a multistakeholder workshop outlining challenges, best practices, and recommendations for AI safety and suicide prevention across model, product, and policy layers.
